title: SmoothQuant integration: quant-profile validator, runtime kernel adapter, and CI calibration matrix
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Summary:
Implement an end-to-end integration for activation-aware INT8 (SmoothQuant) quantization that covers: (1) an automated calibration and quant-profile validator service, (2) a minimal runtime kernel adapter surface so the serving runtime can switch to SmoothQuant-capable kernels, and (3) CI/bench automation to validate accuracy and latency regressions across representative workloads.

Goals:
- Produce per-model, per-layer quantization profiles that include activation rescale factors and per-channel scales when applicable.
- Provide an automated validator that checks quantized model accuracy against a baseline (FP16) and emits a pass/fail signal with detailed per-prompt deltas.
- Expose a kernel adapter abstraction (KernelAdapterV1) that lets the runtime pick SmoothQuant kernels and fall back to reference INT8 kernels when not available.
- Add CI matrix jobs that run calibration on small sample datasets and an accuracy smoke test to catch regressions before rollout.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Calibration harness will run two modes: deterministic offline (full dataset, longer, for release profiles) and lightweight CI (sampled dataset, fast). Deterministic mode writes canonical quant profiles to the profile registry; CI mode validates that profiles meet a permissive accuracy threshold (default: <=0.5% absolute drop on top-1 token next-token prediction over our eval set).
- We prefer per-channel weight scales + a single activation rescale per layer (SmoothQuant pattern) to balance storage and inference efficiency. Per-tensor activation scaling is allowed for very small layers to simplify kernel code paths.
- Latency SLOs: SmoothQuant INT8 paths should stay within +5% median latency of current FP16 baseline on representative sequence lengths. If the kernel cannot meet this, runtime falls back to FP16 or to a higher-precision INT8 kernel with slightly different batching.
- Accuracy monitoring will compute both aggregate metrics and per-prompt distributions; regression alerts will trigger if moving average delta exceeds 0.3% (severity P1).

Implementation tasks (high level):
1) Calibration/Validator Service (team: quant infra)
   - Implement calibration runner that: loads model, runs dataset through forward pass, computes per-layer activation statistics, derives rescale factors, computes per-channel weight scales, serializes a quant-profile JSON.
   - Integrate deterministic mode that records RNG/seed to ensure reproducibility.
   - Validator compares quantized model outputs (using the quant-profile) against FP16 baseline and produces a pass/fail with diffs and summary metrics.
   - Persist profiles to the profile registry with metadata (model version, dataset, seed, date, commit).
2) Runtime Kernel Adapter (team: serving/runtime)
   - Define KernelAdapterV1 interface: list supported ops, an info flag for smoothquant_supported, and a call signature for run_int8_forward(model_key, inputs_ref, kv_handle, quant_profile_id).
   - Implement SmoothQuant kernel variant for key transformer blocks (attention + MLP fused kernels) with activation rescale applied to KV cache and projected matmuls.
   - Implement fallback mechanics: if kernel not available or fails, runtime should automatically fall back to a compatible kernel and record telemetry.
3) CI and Bench Automation (team: infra/ci)
   - Add calibration CI job matrix (small/sampled datasets, representative sequence lengths) that runs on PRs touching runtime/quant code.
   - Add nightly job to run deterministic calibration on a curated set of models and push profiles to staging for manual review.
4) Observability and Rollout
   - Emit metrics: quant_profile_id, calibration_duration_s, validation_accuracy_delta_pct, kernel_selected, fallback_reason.
   - Add dashboard tiles for quant profiles and latest validation runs per model.
   - Rollout plan: feature-flag kernel selection -> internal canary (10% internal traffic 48h) -> enterprise staging (50% traffic 72h) -> full rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Calibration service produces a quant-profile JSON that the runtime can consume and the validator run produces delta metrics.
- KernelAdapterV1 unit tests cover compatibility, signature, and fallback.
- End-to-end smoke test: quantized model serving returns consistent responses with FP16 baseline within configured thresholds on the CI sample set.
- CI matrix detects introduced regressions and blocks merges when accuracy or latency thresholds are exceeded.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for calibration math (scale computation, numerical stability, seed determinism).
- Integration tests: load saved quant profile into a staging runtime and run a small prompt corpus; compare token probabilities and sampling stability against FP16.
- Performance benchmarks: run with realistic batch sizes and sequence lengths; assert latency and throughput within SLO window.
- Chaos test: intentionally corrupt a quant profile to validate graceful fallback and proper alerting.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SmoothQuant+integration+design
- Calibration harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib (branch: eng/ENG-33419)
- Kernel PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218
- Profile registry dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/profile-registry

Security and compliance notes:
- Quant profiles may include layer-level statistics that are model-internal but do not contain raw customer data. Ensure profiles created from customer-provided prompts are not persisted to shared registry unless explicitly opted-in. Add a checkbox in the validator UI for profile persistence.

Rollout checklist (pre-merge / pre-release):
- [ ] Calibration deterministic mode end-to-end run with 3 production models and review by Applied ML.
- [ ] KernelAdapterV1 spec approved by runtime tech lead.
- [ ] CI matrix passing on main for 5 consecutive nightly runs.
- [ ] Telemetry and dashboards live in staging.
- [ ] Security review not required (customer data policy agreed).
